paragraphs: Mentioned in Yevamot 98b [compare 98a]. [1] Ben Yasiyin said, ‘When I went to the coastal cities, I found a certain convert—I said to him, “My son, who permitted you?” He replied, “On this bench R' Akiva sat and said, etc.”’

notes.text: The consulted passage is on Yevamot 98a, while Hyman prints 98b. It concerns permission to marry a maternal brother’s wife, not permission to convert. Hyman omits that detail; the English removes the incorrect conversion gloss without inserting an unquoted clause. The marker [1] remains.

Supplied Yevamot98b remains beside the inherited matching98a comparison; no new whole primary passage was inspected. Who permitted you concerns the permission reported by Akiva, not a new conversion permission. The supplied [1] and וכו׳ remain visible; the missing reference material is not silently supplied. No newly inspected exact full-title occurrence establishes Akiva’s abbreviated R'. No genealogy or footnote clearance follows. The supplied quotation names Ben Yasiyin; neither a former-gentile identity for him nor the unquoted marriage clause is imported into Hyman’s abridged words.

Yevamot 98a names Ben Yasiyin as the narrator and gives the marriage that prompted his question. The ensuing discussion considers the convert’s testimony and offers three grounds for accepting it. Hyman prints 98b and abridges the account. A dark mark near Ben Yasiyin’s name in the scan cannot establish the status or contents of the supplied [1].
